raj: Heads-up — support flagged a customer seeing ~2x token billing for streaming calls when we route to a fallback region + KV cache eviction. Repro notes attached. :eyes:

maria: Ugh. Any reproducible trace?

raj: Minimal. Steps: start a streaming request -> primary region loses route -> client reconnects to fallback -> stream resumes but toolcall was retried and truncated suffix, we ended up attributing both the original and resumed suffix to billing.

kim: Can you paste the router traces? I want to see session-id and any reroute TTL.

raj: Sure, snippet from router logs:
```
INFO route-switch session=abc123 from=us-west to=eu-central reason=capacity
DEBUG stream-resume session=abc123 resume_offset=512 kv_hit=false toolcalls=[{"id":"tool-42","state":"inflight","seq":8}]
WARN toolcall-retry session=abc123 tool=tool-42 retry_reason=client-reconnect truncation_detected=true
```

ana: (typo: ana) If kv_hit=false that means prefix wasn't cached on fallback and we re-sent prefix -> double-charge?

raj: That's the hypothesis. The original toolcall had partial tokens captured in the ledger when we lost connectivity; on resume the system retried the toolcall without seeing the provisional ledger entry from the primary. Router routed to a different shard which didn't have the provisional entry, so the ledger confirmed both attempts.

maria: Does our provisional billing flow use a per-session provisional id or per-route provisional_id? If per-route then different shards won't dedupe.

kim: It's per-shard keyed by (session_id, shard_id, prefix_hash) currently. We discussed global provisional IDs but avoided complexity.

raj: Right — so cross-shard routing breaks dedupe. Also truncation detection is noisy: when streaming truncates we sometimes mark a toolcall as "incomplete" and later as "retry" instead of "resume". That flips heuristics used by billing.

josh: Can we short-term mitigate by tightening the router sticky-window for resume? If we keep affinity for, say, 30s we might avoid cross-shard routing on reconnects for the same session.

ana: That helps for reconnects from same region but not for planned failover or autoscaling evictions. Also stashing provisional ledger in a cross-shard store would be safer.

maria: Query I ran against clickhouse to find examples (rolled into a single row per session):
```
SELECT session_id, countDistinct(provisional_id) AS provisional_count, sum(tokens) AS billed_tokens
FROM billing_events
WHERE event_time > now() - INTERVAL 7 day
AND session_prefix = 'q1'
GROUP BY session_id
HAVING provisional_count > 1
ORDER BY billed_tokens DESC
LIMIT 50
```

maria: We see ~120 sessions in last week with >1 provisional_id and same final request path. Most correlate with route-switch events.

kim: Ok. Proposed plan:
- short-term: bump router session affinity to 45s for streaming sessions (can be toggled by feature flag)
- mid-term: create a cross-shard provisional index (small KV) that stores provisional_id -> canonical_attempt_id with TTL 5m
- long-term: refactor provisional ledger to be global or implement causal replication across shards

raj: +1. Also add a console alert/telemetry: metric for provisional_count_per_session and a dashboard showing sessions with >1 provisional and route-switch rate. That will help triage upstream customers.

ana: For the mid-term cross-shard KV, watch out for perf: heavy write rate on hot prefixes could blow up. We should shard the index by prefix_hash and use async replication path to avoid tail latency coupling.

josh: For immediate customer relief, we can offer a quota credit while we patch. Ops can run a one-off script to reconcile obvious double-charges (same session, overlapping token ranges). I can draft a reconciliation query.

maria: Also add one more defensive heuristic in billing: if a provisional appears on two different shards within 2 minutes for same session+prefix, mark it provisional_dupe=true and don't finalize until manual review or after TTL. That reduces autoposting charges.

raj: Good idea. Will open an RFC and a tiny PR for the affinity flag. I'll attach repro harness and the clickhouse query. Deploy-bot: can we schedule a canary of the affinity toggle to 10% of streaming traffic?

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: feature-flag:router-affinity-45s -> canary=10% -> start=1744016000 -> notify=#eng-oncall on completion

kim: I'll own the provisional-index spike (mid-term). I'll add benchmarks.

ana: I'll draft the console dashboard tiles (provisional_count, route-switch rate, avg-resume-latency).

raj: Thanks. Keeping this thread as the action tracker.

maria: Quick note: make sure we include toolcall ids in telemetry; otherwise manual reconciliation is painful.

josh: I'll own reconciliation script; ping me when you have the query.

raj: pinged all owners in Asana. I'll update when we have canary metrics. :thumbsup:
